topStories.headline: SFSU President Lynn Mahoney Announces She Will Retire Next Summer
topStories.dek: Mahoney, the first woman to serve as SFSU's permanent president, will step down after nine years leading the university while the CSU Board of Trustees conducts a national search for her successor.
topStories.body:
San Francisco State University President Lynn Mahoney announced on September 8 that she will retire next summer after nine years leading the university and 19 years of total service to the California State University system. Mahoney took office in July 2019 and is the 14th — and first permanent female — president of SFSU.

Mahoney said she will remain in the role while the CSU Board of Trustees conducts a national search for her successor. In her message to the campus community, she described the decision as deeply personal, citing her wish to devote more time to her growing family.

The announcement drew wide media coverage — including reports on KQED, KTVU-TV, KRON-TV, and KGO-TV — and generated what the Golden Gate Xpress, SFSU's student newspaper, described as mixed emotions from staff and students on the Lakeshore campus. The paper published a full reaction piece the same day the announcement broke.

Mahoney's tenure has included steering the campus through the COVID-19 pandemic, a renewed push on enrollment growth, and a fall-semester visit by Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi to tour new science and engineering and student housing facilities. Under her leadership, the university was recently recognized by The Wall Street Journal as one of the top 25 schools in the nation for social mobility.

topStories.headline: West Portal Elementary Turns 100 — and the Neighborhood Is Throwing a Block Party on October 3
topStories.dek: The school's centennial celebration will fill West Portal Avenue from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., starting at the branch library courtyard.
topStories.body:
West Portal Elementary School is marking its 100th year with a community celebration on Saturday, October 3, from 11:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. along West Portal Avenue. The event begins at the West Portal Branch Library courtyard, according to a notice posted September 13 by the Greater West Portal Neighborhood Association.

Organizers are encouraging families throughout the neighborhood to attend the all-ages, street-level event. The school sits one block from the West Portal Muni station, which serves roughly 5,000 daily boarders and anchors a commercial corridor often described as a village inside the city.

Details about specific programming were not published with the initial announcement; the GWPNA directed residents to a QR code on neighborhood flyers for additional information. The West Portal Branch Library — which also sits a block from the Muni station — will serve as the gathering point for the celebration.

topStories.headline: SFMTA: Injury Crashes Near West Portal Station Are Down 60 Percent Since 2024 Safety Redesign
topStories.dek: A June 2026 SFMTA evaluation report confirms that the quick-build overhaul triggered by a fatal 2024 crash has sharply reduced collisions, and decorative crosswalk installation was still underway as of the week of September 2.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency has completed its formal evaluation of the West Portal Station Safety and Community Space Improvements project, concluding that the traffic redesign put in place in fall 2024 has made the streets around the station substantially safer. The final evaluation report was published in June 2026.

Traffic collision rates in the half-square-mile area around the West Portal Muni station dropped 60 percent between October 2024 and March 2026, compared to the equivalent period before the project (October 2022 to March 2024). Serious injury crashes fell from an average of 6.7 per year to 2.7 per year. SFMTA monitoring also found that fewer than 1 percent of drivers on Ulloa and Vicente streets were traveling five or more miles per hour above the speed limit.

The safety changes were spurred by the March 2024 deaths of Matilde Ramos Pinto, Diego Cardoso de Oliveira, and their two children, who were struck by a vehicle while waiting at the bus stop in front of the West Portal Branch Library. The quick-build redesign included transit-priority lanes, turn restrictions, a repaved pedestrian horseshoe plaza at the station entrance, a street mural, a bikeshare station, and planters.

Work continued into this month: SFMTA announced that decorative crosswalk installation — the final beautification element of the quick-build phase — was rescheduled to begin the week of September 2. The agency has said it will use data from the current installation to evaluate whether more permanent materials are warranted in a future redesign.

moreNews.headline: Parkmerced Remains Under Receivership 18 Months After $1.8 Billion Default
moreNews.body: Parkmerced, the 3,165-unit apartment complex near Lake Merced and SFSU, has been under court-appointed receivership since March 6, 2025, after owner Maximus Real Estate Partners defaulted on $1.8 billion in loans. A San Francisco Superior Court judge placed Douglas Wilson Companies in control following a motion by lenders Barclays and Citigroup. Day-to-day management was assigned to Brick + Timber, the property management arm of SF-based Ballast Investments, which committed to a $70 million renovation addressing inoperable elevators, water intrusion, mold, and lighting deficiencies across the complex's roughly 8,000-resident community. As of an SF Standard report from November 2025, some residents said conditions had not materially improved; the receiver has stated that no sale of the property is expected in the near term.

moreNews.headline: Fundraiser Underway for Memorial Statue at West Portal Library Honoring Family Killed at Bus Stop
moreNews.body: The nonprofit Livable City is raising funds for a permanent memorial statue to be placed outside the West Portal Branch Library, honoring Matilde Ramos Pinto, Diego Cardoso de Oliveira, and their two children — the family killed when a vehicle struck them at the library bus stop in March 2024. The project is noted on the West Portal Branch Library's official SFPL page; no completion date has been publicly announced. The 2024 crash also directly prompted the SFMTA safety redesign at West Portal Station whose results are reported in this week's lead stories.
